I applied every assignment in order, keeping a running value for each variable and reducing mod 100 after each addition. Two points mattered beyond the routine additions:
- `b` is reset to 46 early on (its second assignment). Its starting value of 87 therefore plays no part in the result.
- `TMP` starts at 7 and from then on only receives additions.

The full trace is too long to reproduce. Here are the opening steps to show the method:

| Step | Assignment | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | TMP ← (7 + 9) mod 100 | TMP = 16 |
| 2 | b ← 46 | b = 46 |
| 3 | TMP ← (16 + 95) mod 100 | TMP = 11 |
| 4 | e ← (11 + 35) mod 100 | e = 46 |
| 5 | b ← (46 + 65) mod 100 | b = 11 |
| 6 | TMP ← (11 + 84) mod 100 | TMP = 95 |
| 7 | d ← (95 + 59) mod 100 | d = 54 |
| 8 | h ← (54 + 41) mod 100 | h = 95 |

The final assignments of the program are:
- f ← (54 + 12) = 66
- b ← (66 + 88) mod 100 = 54
- TMP ← (54 + 87) mod 100 = 41
- d ← (41 + 75) mod 100 = 16
- c ← (16 + 25) = 41

Final values:
- a = 46
- b = 54
- c = 41
- d = 16
- e = 95
- f = 66
- g = 12
- h = 11
- TMP = 41
